precepts.text: Nahshon the son of Amminadab was captain of the children of Judah; these were princes and captains, not ordinary men, and Boaz came from that line.
precepts.point: Hezron begat Ram, Ram begat Amminadab, Amminadab begat Nahshon the prince of the children of Judah, and from Nahshon come Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

precepts.text: On the east side toward the rising of the sun pitch the standard of the camp of Judah, with Issachar and Zebulun beside him.
precepts.point: When the alarm is blown the second time, the camps that lie on the south side take their journey: that was Reuben, Simeon, and Gad. The alarm for the journeys was short bursts.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
“When ye blow an alarm, then the camps that lie on the east parts shall go forward.” Numbers 2 shows who lay on the east parts. “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.” Next to him pitched “the tribe of Issachar: and Nethaneel the son of Zuar shall be captain”, and “Then the tribe of Zebulun: and Eliab the son of Helon shall be captain of the children of Zebulun.”

So the camps that went forward first at the alarm were Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, under the standard of the camp of Judah. The alarm for the journeys was short bursts, and at the first alarm the east side, the camp of Judah, took the lead.

precepts.text: On the south side is the standard of the camp of Reuben, with Simeon and Gad beside him.
precepts.point: When the alarm is blown the second time, the camps that lie on the south side take their journey: that was Reuben, Simeon, and Gad. The alarm for the journeys was short bursts.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
“When ye blow an alarm the second time, then the camps that lie on the south side shall take their journey.” Numbers 2 names the south side. “On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben according to their armies: and the captain of the children of Reuben shall be Elizur the son of Shedeur.” Those which pitched by him were “the tribe of Simeon: and the captain of the children of Simeon shall be Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai”, and “Then the tribe of Gad: and the captain of the sons of Gad shall be Eliasaph the son of Reuel.”

So at the second alarm Reuben, Simeon, and Gad took their journey, under the standard of the camp of Reuben. Each alarm of short bursts moved the next side of the camp in order: “they shall blow an alarm for their journeys.”

points: Every man of the children of Israel pitched by his own standard, with the ensign of his father's house, far off about the tabernacle of the congregation.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: On the east side toward the rising of the sun pitched the standard of the camp of Judah, with Nahshon the son of Amminadab as captain, and next to him Issachar under Nethaneel the son of Zuar and Zebulun under Eliab the son of Helon.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: All that were numbered in the camp of Judah were an hundred thousand and fourscore thousand and six thousand and four hundred, which is 186,400 throughout their armies; and these set forth first.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: On the south side was the standard of the camp of Reuben, with Elizur the son of Shedeur as captain, and by him Simeon under Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai and Gad under Eliasaph the son of Reuel.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: All that were numbered in the camp of Reuben were an hundred thousand and fifty and one thousand and four hundred and fifty, which is 151,450 throughout their armies; and they set forth in the second rank.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: Then the tabernacle of the congregation set forward with the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camp: as they encamped, so they set forward, every man in his place by their standards.
The tabernacle stayed in the middle of the formation whether Israel was camped or marching; the order of the camp was the order of the march.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: On the west side was the standard of the camp of Ephraim, with Elishama the son of Ammihud as captain, and by him Manasseh under Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur and Benjamin under Abidan the son of Gideoni.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: All that were numbered of the camp of Ephraim were an hundred thousand and eight thousand and an hundred, which is 108,100 throughout their armies; and they went forward in the third rank.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: On the north side was the standard of the camp of Dan, with Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai as captain, and by him Asher under Pagiel the son of Ocran and Naphtali under Ahira the son of Enan.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: All that were numbered of the camp of Dan were an hundred thousand and fifty and seven thousand and six hundred, which is 157,600; and they went hindmost with their standards.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: All those that were numbered of the camps throughout their hosts were six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty; but the Levites were not numbered among the children of Israel, as the Most High commanded Moses.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: The children of Israel did according to all that the Most High commanded Moses: so they pitched by their standards, and so they set forward, every one after their families, according to the house of their fathers.
